model: none - no image model was called and nothing was spent
graded_note: A6b, grade once. The two fields say the two different things that get confused: the cells DO carry the ingest grade (graded: true, which is what the frame manifest records), and this run did not apply it (graded_in_this_run: false). It was applied once, upstream, to float-eye.webp in 2026-07. Re-running it here would darken the cells a second time and, worse, grayscale: true would flatten the corona that is the whole read of the attack frame.
license_note: Derived from float-eye.webp, an owner-supplied external illustration (no source traced). T, 2026-10-29, D115: "The images we use for everything are open source."
source: art-department/masters/enemies/float-eye.sheet.png (2048x768 lossless master, 8 columns x 3 rows of 256px cells; see its own provenance.json, which records the rig that drew it)
method: The master was cut into 24 lossless PNG cells by the splitter, row-major, then each cell was encoded to WebP q44 by the shared ingest recipe with the grade skipped. Every pixel descends from the shipped painting; the sheet master itself never enters this tree (D98).
used_by: components/combat/encounter/CombatCombatantPane.tsx - the enemy figure in live combat
measured: A11, measured on these exact files: 24 cells, 156452 B (152.8 KB) in total, mean 6519 B, max 9352 B (float-eye-20.webp, the attack flare), min 3786 B - against 23624 B for the static float-eye.webp. 6.6x, +132.8 KB for one enemy. FRAME_CELL_MAX_BYTES is 12000 and frame-cells.test.mjs fails any cell above it, so a regenerated set cannot quietly triple.
portrait_note: A7 (phase AN5a): the SHA-256 of the static portrait this set was drawn from. scripts/frame-set-portraits.test.mjs (root npm test) fails when the portrait's bytes no longer match: a swapped portrait retires this set (remove it or regenerate it from the new portrait).
